{{nihongo|'''Iko-no-hayamitama Hime-no Shrine'''|伊古乃速御玉比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Iko no Hayamitamahime Shrine''' (いこのはやみたまひめじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located along the {{ill|Namegawa|Q11565004|qid=Q11565004|lt=Namegawa}} in {{ill|Namegawa, Saitama|Q1346985|qid=Q1346985}}, {{ill|Hiki District, Saitama|Q1075201|qid=Q1075201}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. The enshrined deities are {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Ōtomowake no Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}. The original enshrined deity, as indicated by the shrine’s name, is Hayamitamahime no Mikoto. It is one of the candidate shrines for the minor {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Minor Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}} {{ill|Chichibu District, Saitama|Q1145581|qid=Q1145581}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
'''Iko no Hayamitamahime Shrine (Okumiya)'''

It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ninken|Q357266|qid=Q357266}} (449–460) by descendants of {{ill|Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune|Q11625205|qid=Q11625205|lt=Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune}} on the summit of Mount Ninomiyama. <ref name="Shrine notice board">From the shrine notice board</ref> In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 4 (1576), the shrine was relocated to its present location, and the shrine on Mount Ninomiyama became the Okumiya (inner shrine). In addition, Haruna Shrine was enshrined together at the Okumiya in prayers for abundant harvests.

'''Iko no Hayamitamahime Shrine (Hongū)'''

The main hall of the Hongū enshrines Inari Ōkami and Atago Ōkami together as auxiliary deities {{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki}}.
This shrine was also known by the alternate name Awazu Myōjin. The “su” (洲) of Awazu Myōjin is thought to mean “island” in Saitama Prefecture, and it is believed that a divided spirit of {{ill|Awashima-no-Kami|Q1575740|qid=Q1575740|lt=Awashima deity}}, the enshrined deity of Kada Shrine (now {{ill|Awashima Shrine (Wakayama)|Q7007362|qid=Q7007362}}) located at Kada-no-ura in {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053}} {{ill|Kaisō District, Wakayama|Q1130990|qid=Q1130990}}, was transferred here. <ref name="Saitama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines">From “Shrines of Saitama: Ōsato, Kita-Katsushika, and Hiki” (Publisher: Saitama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines, July 1992)</ref>

: (Founded) {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 2 (1395)

: (Enshrined deities) {{ill|Yakusanoikazuchi|Q10892534|qid=Q10892534}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}}

: (Founded) during the {{ill|Einin|Q1327307|qid=Q1327307}} era (1293–1298) at a place called Oyama-no-dai. Relocated to the present site in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 1 (1624).

* Tarōmaru, Ranzan Town – Awazu Shrine<ref name="Saitama Prefecture Shrine Register">From Saitama Prefecture “Shrine Register” (Home Ministry, 1878), Awazu Shrine, Tarōmaru, Nanagō Village</ref>
: (Enshrined deity) Hayamitamahime no Mikoto
: (Founded) Genroku 8 (1695)
: (Notes) A divided spirit from the Awazu Myōjin Shrine of Mizubusa Village (present-day Awasu Shrine)
* Katsuta, Ranzan Town – Awazu Shrine
: (Enshrined deities) {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Ōtomowake no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune}}

* Hachiman Shrine
: The Hachiman Shrine formerly located in the area called Gōshamae was merged with the precinct Atago Shrine and renamed to its current shrine name. <ref name="Namegawa Village History: Folklore Volume" />
* Kotohira Shrine
* Tenman Tenjin Shrine

=== Access ===
* From {{ill|Tōbu Tōjō Lines|Q11527536|qid=Q11527536}} {{ill|Shinrin-kōen Station (Saitama)|Q5368656|qid=Q5368656|lt=Shinrin-Kōen Station}}, take the Kokusai Jūō Kōtsū bus bound for “Kumagaya Station South Exit.” Get off at the “Shinrin-Kōen South Exit” bus stop, then walk 30 minutes (2.8 km).
